title: Chicken Tinga
subtitle: Shredded chicken in a smoky tomato sauce
excerpt: Chicken tinga is a classic Mexican preparation of shredded chicken simmered in a smoky tomato and chilli sauce. It piles brilliantly into tacos, burritos or tostadas and comes together from pantry ingredients in well under an hour.
sourceNotes: Chicken tinga originates in Puebla, Mexico, where it is traditionally made with chipotle peppers in adobo sauce. The smoky heat of chipotle is central to the dish; smoked paprika and chilli flakes make a workable substitute when chipotle is unavailable.

content.text: Traditional tinga uses chipotle in adobo. This version uses smoked paprika and chilli flakes for a similar smoky heat from pantry staples. If you have chipotle paste, swap both for 1 to 2 tablespoons of it.

items.prepNote: poached in salted water until cooked, then shredded

content.text: Simmer the chicken breasts in a pot of salted water for 15 minutes until cooked through. Remove and shred into coarse strips with two forks. Set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic, smoked paprika, chilli flakes, cumin and oregano. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the shredded chicken and stir to coat in the sauce. Cook for 5 minutes until the chicken is heated through and has soaked up the sauce. Season with salt.

items.fix: Poach on a low simmer and remove as soon as cooked through.

items.symptom: Sauce tastes flat and lacks smokiness.
items.cause: Smoked paprika was too old and has lost its potency.
items.fix: Use fresh smoked paprika or add a pinch more to taste.
